segmentation: The instance-segmentation view separates as many as four pedestrians and one handbag from the otherwise unsegmented plaza. It follows the main woman, shown with a pink mask, as she turns toward the camera wearer and moves from approximately 8–10 m ahead on the left in frame 1 to the bottom center in frame 5, about 0.5–0.8 m away and within arm's reach, with the lower image edge cutting off her torso and raised hands. A far-left pedestrian with a cyan/green mask, around 7–9 m away and 3–4 m left of the woman, exits through the left edge after frame 4, while a right-side pedestrian with a brown mask, approximately 6–10 m distant and 4–6 m to her right, moves toward the right edge. Relative to RGB alone, this map makes the poorly illuminated background pedestrians in frames 1–2 easier to identify and more clearly reveals when the companion disappears behind the woman. Still, it is unreliable because it labels the strap and front of her dress as a large green handbag over her chest in frames 3–4, splits the companion across overlapping 'person' labels in frame 2, fails to capture the companion's faintly visible shoulder behind her in frame 5, and omits every architectural obstacle, including the pillars and foreground bush.
pose: The pose visualization contains no detections in frames 1–3, when every pedestrian is about 4–10 m away, and produces a body skeleton only after the main woman reaches roughly 2 m in frame 4 and approximately 0.5–0.8 m in frame 5, placing her within the camera wearer's arm's reach.
